messages:
elaine-cs: Heads up — enterprise customer (acct: 12345) opened a ticket: sudden spike in 5xxs + 2000ms p95. They say requests from EU users are routed to us-east, added cross-region latency and higher bill. Attaching their sample req IDs: req_abc123, req_def456.

customer-ops: Confirming — we saw 503 / 504 and very high token latency starting 2026-03-16T22:10Z. All traffic normally lives in eu-west-1.

routing-bot: [alert] auto-spillover executed for eu-west-1 at 2026-03-16T22:09:03Z. Policy=region-capacity-exhaustion, action=spillover, fallback_regions=[us-east-1,ap-southeast-1], initial_fraction=0.10, observed_error_rate=0.18

oliver-sre: Thanks, sending quick repro checklist — can you paste raw request headers + the x-request-id trace for one example? Also include the routing decision trace from our side if available.

elaine-cs: Pasting one sample (redacted):

```
x-request-id: req_abc123
x-customer-id: 12345
x-client-region: eu-west-1
x-forwarded-for: 35.194.12.8
```

Client sees 503 and then a 200 with 1400ms, response headers show `x-served-region: us-east-1` even though client pref is eu-west-1.

mike-runtime: I pulled the routing trace for req_abc123 — on our side the region pool for eu-west-1 hit max_queue_depth and the shard responded with `spillover=true` then route decision picked us-east-1 replica (latency/capacity tradeoff). Shows up as `decision_chain: eu-west-1 -> fallback(us-east-1)` in logs.

oliver-sre: Can you also share which model variant they were hitting and if they had pinned versions? Spillover should prefer same-region compatible variants before going cross-region.

customer-ops: They were on model=rwd-13b-v1, not region-pinned. No canary or pin.

mike-runtime: Two mitigation options: (1) temporary tenant pin via admin API to force eu-west-1 routing for this tenant; (2) reduce global spillover fraction / increase prefer_same_region weight so routing tries local warm replicas first. Quick command to pin:

```
POST https://admin.internal/v1/tenants/12345/pinning
Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN
Body: { "pin_region": "eu-west-1", "duration": 3600 }
```

(Requires admin perms).

james-billing: FYI customer reported unexpected inter-region egress charges due to spillover. Recommend we pre-authorize a credit while we triage. I'll prepare a small one-time credit proposal; need cost delta estimate from infra.

oliver-sre: I'll run a quick check on eu-west-1 capacity history — looks like a short term saturation caused by a large batched job from another tenant + autoscaler delay. Root cause: queue depth exceeded soft threshold, triggering spillover. We should throttle large batch jobs more aggressively.

elaine-cs: Customer asked for repro steps so they can validate fix on their side. Suggested steps I gave: (1) curl their usual endpoint with header `x-redwood-region: eu-west-1` to see if we honor it; (2) send a few parallel requests and observe `x-served-region`. They tried `x-redwood-region` and got mixed results.

mike-runtime: Important note: header override honors tenant pinning and routing policy only if tenant has `allow_client_region_override` enabled. We should check tenant config. If it's disabled, header is ignored and routing decisions are purely server-side.

oliver-sre: Immediate remediation I applied: set tenant 12345 prefer_same_region=true and reduced spillover initial_fraction from 0.10 -> 0.02 for the eu-west-1 policy. I ran the admin API call at 22:12Z.

routing-bot: [notice] routing policy update applied for tenant 12345 by oliver-sre at 2026-03-16T22:12:14Z. prefer_same_region=true, spillover_fraction=0.02

customer-ops: After the change we see p95 drop to ~220ms and errors dropped to baseline. Customer confirms latency is back to normal.

james-billing: I'll queue the credit approval. Please capture the exact cross-region token/egress delta for the billing ticket.

oliver-sre: Follow-ups: (a) add a runbook entry for short-term surge throttling and tenant pinning steps; (b) investigate autoscaler hysteresis that created the delay; (c) evaluate changing default spillover policy to prefer local warm replicas first. I'll assign tasks in the runbook.

elaine-cs: Thanks team — forwarding resolution to customer and marking ticket high-priority follow-up.

mike-runtime: One more: add a routing metric export for 'spillover_fraction' per-policy so we can alert earlier when fraction > 0.05 for >30s.

oliver-sre: Agreed. I'll open an infra ticket.

customer-ops: Confirmed from customer: no additional functional issues; will reach out if anything else crops up. :thumbsup:
